headline: Payrolls 162k beat every estimate, July's -23k revised to +21k, September hike back near 58%
stance: July's -23k is now +21k, August landed at 162k, and the September hike is priced back near 58%. Oil at a six-week high and Canadian tariffs from 12:01am land on the same session.

news.head: Payrolls 162k, above every estimate
news.body: August beat a +58k consensus. June and July were revised up 55k combined; July's -23k became +21k. Unemployment held 4.1%, earnings +3.1% y/y.

news.head: US and Iran traded strikes over the weekend
news.body: The US hit three Iranian tankers Saturday, the IRGC claimed six vessels, and Aramco's Jizan refinery was struck again. Hormuz traffic is ~10 ships a day.

news.head: Canadian tariffs live at 12:01am ET
news.body: 15-50% on ~$20bn of US goods across 700-plus lines: steel, machinery, farm equipment, appliances, dairy. Carney is matching Washington dollar for dollar.

news.head: Yen strongest since February on BoJ
news.body: USD/JPY through 154 overnight (~2am ET), strongest since Feb 23. A 25bp BoJ hike on Sep 18 is largely priced; the guidance after it is the question.

implications: Two inflation prints stand between Friday's 162k and the FOMC, Sep 16. A hot pair on top of $97 Brent ends the coin flip.
Information payrolls fell 23,000 in August, in computing infrastructure and publishing. The labor data is telling a different AI story than the capex is.

watch.head: Whether the front end finishes the repricing
watch.body: Friday's 100k beat barely moved the front end. A meeting priced near 58% and a 2y that shrugged cannot both be right.

watch.head: Brent, and whether Hormuz traffic recovers
watch.body: Roughly a fifth of the world's oil moves through the strait in peacetime. Ten commodity ships a day crossed over the last ten days.

watch.head: Consumer credit, 3:00
watch.body: The only US release today. Revolving balances are the read on whether the household is funding spending or earning it.

watch.head: PPI, Sep 10
watch.body: Producer prices are the first of two inflation reads before the meeting. Consumer prices follow Friday.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: July's -23k is now +21k. The print the dovish case rested on was a revision artifact.
Waller wanted disinflation given a chance. Earnings ran 3.1% y/y and 0.3% on the month.
Food services added 59k of the 162k, local government education 42k. Information lost 23k.
sections.positioning: Spec is long the 2-year at the 99th percentile of three years, a sixth straight week. An extended long, into a meeting the same market now prices near 58% for a hike.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Dow futures -0.6%, Nasdaq-100 +0.1% overnight (~3am ET). The tariff list is steel, machinery, appliances, not software.
A 100k payroll beat cost the S&P less than half a percent Friday. Equities are treating the hike as survivable.
Energy is the only sector with a live catalyst this morning. Brent $97.50, +0.5% (~3am ET).
sections.positioning: Spec is short the Russell at the 2nd percentile of three years, a nineteenth straight week. Standing background, and small caps carry the tariff and the rate risk both.

single_name.note: Liberty Latin America joined the list Friday on an insider buy filed the same day, $476k. Three filings, above its 200-day, 1.95 days to cover.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: Investment-grade and high-yield spreads are still marked to Thursday. Credit has not priced the payroll number at all.
Equity-credit correlation at 0.63, down from 0.66. The two are drifting apart into the meeting.
Bank credit is growing 5.96% y/y. Lending is expanding into a tightening the market is 58% sure of.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer investment-grade inventory sits at the 21st percentile of its three-year range. Dealers are carrying little into next week's meeting.
